name: Undersea cables & GPS
summary: Finnish court convicts crew over Baltic cable damage; Iranian threats to Gulf cables stand
state: A Finnish court on 5 Nov found a Russian captain and another crew member guilty of damaging Baltic Sea cables (Washington Times). Iranian officials suggested on 4 Nov that Gulf undersea cables could be targeted. GNSS jamming remains widespread in the Gulf and Baltic. No new cable cut was reported as of 5 Nov.
for_you: Internet users in the Gulf and Baltic may see slowdowns if cables are cut; no action needed now.
rubric_hit: Threats and jamming without new cuts = Watch

sources.title: Washington Times — Russian captain among crew found guilty of damaging Baltic cables

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
